title: fix(components,fields): honour a declared character cap on the built-in textarea branch (#3439)
body:
Fixes #3439

One `maxLength` declaration produced two experiences. The registered `field:textarea` widget ships four affordances; the form renderer's built-in, unregistered `textarea` branch shipped a subset of one of them.

## The card's unverified half, measured first

The filer explicitly did not trace whether `maxLength` reaches the built-in branch's element, and flagged that `stripRendererOnlyProps(fieldProps)` might already deliver it via `rest`. Measured on `origin/main` @ `feb6b161d` with a throwaway probe that rendered the built-in branch and dumped the element's attributes. **The answer splits by spelling**, which is why this PR is wider than the visible counter:

| authored | `maxlength` attribute | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `maxLength: 100` | `"100"` | hard truncation worked — **by coincidence** |
| `max_length: 100` | `null`, plus a stray `max_length="100"` | **no cap at all** |

The camelCase spelling worked only because it happens to name a real DOM attribute and the branch spreads leftover field props onto the element. **Nothing read the cap**, so the legacy `max_length` spelling — dual-read by the registered widget since framework#1878 §3, and by all three producers of a form field (`ObjectForm`, `sectionFields`, `EmbeddableForm.applyDefaultMaxLengths`) — landed as an inert attribute and capped nothing.

So the gap was: the counter, the accessible limit, **and** hard truncation for one of the two authored spellings.

## What the parity had to cover, and does

All four affordances now render on **both** of the branch's surfaces (inline control and fullscreen dialog):

1. native `maxLength` hard truncation — now resolved from both spellings;
2. the visible `{n}/{max}` count, `aria-hidden`;
3. a description node wired through `aria-describedby`, so the limit is announced **on focus**;
4. a threshold-gated, debounced `aria-live="polite"` near-limit notice (inline only).

Items 3 and 4 are the point. A screen-reader user on this path previously learned the limit only as a validation error *after* submitting. Shipping the visible digits alone would have fixed the sighted half and left the accessibility half exactly as broken — Leg A below exists to prove the suite can tell those two halves apart.

## The hoist

`CharacterCount` moved from `packages/fields/src/widgets/CharacterCount.tsx` to `packages/components/src/custom/character-count.tsx`, mirroring PR #4193 rather than inventing a second hoist. Same measured graph, re-checked on this tip: `packages/fields/package.json` depends on `@object-ui/components`; `packages/components/package.json` names `@object-ui/fields` in neither `dependencies` nor `peerDependencies`. One-way edge, ruled direction legal.

**Published-surface watch item, answered: nothing was removed or relocated.** `CharacterCount` was never exported from the `@object-ui/fields` barrel (`packages/fields/src/index.tsx` re-exports `./widgets/TextAreaField`, never `./widgets/CharacterCount`), and its only consumer was `TextAreaField` inside that same package. So no `@object-ui/fields` consumer can break, and **no re-export was added there** — publishing one would mint a public export of `@object-ui/fields` that never existed, which is the `toggleClassName` reasoning from #4193 applied in reverse. It is a **new, additive** export of `@object-ui/components`, reachable through `export * from './custom'`.

The copy moved with the implementation onto the same `fields.textarea.*` keys with byte-identical English defaults, exactly as #4193 did for `form.fullscreen.*` — so the ten locale packs need no edit and provider-less rendering is unchanged.

## Why the built-in branch got parity rather than a documented trade-off

The dispatch's fork clause asked for a **recorded** lean-fallback rationale, not an inference from thin code. There is none: repo-wide search for one returned nothing, and the record rules the other way — the maintainer's 2026-08-10 ruling on #3398 ("one implementation, hoisted to the dependency-legal side"), plus #3272, #3393, #3400, #3402 and #4824, which each brought this same branch toward parity. The standing line applies: one form-level declaration must produce one behaviour on both render paths.

## Notes on shape

- **`BuiltinTextarea` is a component, not inline JSX.** The counter needs a positioned wrapper, and `FormControl` is a Radix `Slot` that injects `id` / `aria-describedby` / `aria-invalid` into whatever element the branch returns. Returning a wrapper `div` directly would hand those three to the div and leave the control with no accessible name and a dangling label `for` — objectui#3976 exactly. A component boundary receives them as props and re-addresses them onto the `textarea`. Same reason `BuiltinSelectControl` is a component.
- **`aria-describedby` is APPENDED, never assigned**, on both inline surfaces — assigning would trade "no cap announced" for "no error announced". The dialog editor assigns, because its ids are built from scratch and the host's ids name nodes Radix `aria-hidden`s while the modal is open.
- **Two description ids per widget instance.** The dialog edits a local draft, so the two surfaces count different strings; one shared id would point both controls at whichever sentence rendered last.
- **A field with no cap renders exactly what it rendered before** — no wrapper, no counter, no live region.
- **`max_length` is kept off the DOM.** It is not a DOM attribute in any spelling; left in the pass-through it renders invalid HTML that reads like a working cap.

## Verification

All commands from the repo root, each heavy run serialized on the shared container lock.

Targeted suites (the two new files, 22 cases):

```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  22 passed (22)
```

Affected packages — `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/components/ packages/fields/ packages/i18n/`:

```
Test Files  312 passed (312)
     Tests  4081 passed (4081)
```

`packages/plugin-form/` (the built-in branch's producer and consumer):

```
Test Files  55 passed (55)
     Tests  571 passed (571)
```

Type-check: `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/fields`, `@object-ui/i18n` all Done. Lint: components 0 errors / 882 warnings, fields 0 errors / 814 warnings — all warnings pre-existing. `check-changeset-presence` and `check-control-bytes` green, plus a targeted control-byte grep over the changed files.

### Reverse verification (three legs, all in the predicted direction)

Each leg was mutated from the **committed** state and restored by checking the file back out of the branch (`git checkout` of the branch ref, per-path); `git status` was empty after every restore.

A note on rebuilds, because it changes what these legs prove: this repo's `vitest.config.mts` aliases every `@object-ui/*` specifier back to that package's `src`, so **vitest legs are source-resolved and need no `dist` rebuild**. `tsc` does not use that alias — it resolves through package `exports` to `dist/*.d.ts` — so Leg C alone required one, and it got one.

1. **Delete the description node's `id`** in the hoisted `CharacterCount` (breaks affordance 3 for both render paths) — **7 failed / 15 passed**. The failures are exactly the accessibility assertions (`reaches the control through aria-describedby`, `APPENDS to the description the form already supplied`, the dialog's own-draft sentence, both locale legs); every visible-digits assertion stayed green. That asymmetry is the point: this is the "ship the sighted half" shape, and the suite distinguishes it. Restored.
2. **Drop the legacy `max_length` read** at the call site — **exactly 2 failed**, both legacy-spelling cases. `never leaks max_length onto the DOM` stayed green, as predicted: the DOM strip is independent of the resolution, so the two concerns are pinned separately. Restored.
3. **Cross-package type change**: after rebuilding `@object-ui/components` (`dist/custom/character-count.d.ts` regenerated), pasting an undeclared prop onto the `CharacterCount` call site in `packages/fields` is REJECTED — `error TS2322: … not assignable to type 'IntrinsicAttributes & CharacterCountProps'` — which is what proves `tsc` read the rebuilt `.d.ts` rather than a cached one. Restored; `fields` type-check green again.

## Out of scope

The built-in **`input`** branch has the identical split, measured the same way: `maxLength: 50` gives `maxlength="50"`, `max_length: 50` gives `maxlength: null` plus a stray `max_length` attribute. Same mechanism, same file, different branch — and whether a single-line input should also carry a counter is a separate design call rather than a mechanical repeat. Filed separately, unassigned; it is not addressed here.
